history.dynasty: None (modern; built and managed by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams)
history.summary: The Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple at Rushikonda, inaugurated as the Sri Venkateswara Divya Kshetram, is the flagship TTD temple of Visakhapatnam. Built by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams at a cost of about Rs. 28 crore on 10 acres atop a hill overlooking the Bay of Bengal, it was constructed between 2020 and 2022 as part of TTD's mission to build over 1,000 Srivari temples across India from Kashmir to Kanyakumari. The Maha Samprokshana (grand consecration) was held over six days from 18-23 March 2022, and a grand Maha Kumbhabhishekam was conducted in March 2023 led by the Visakha Sarada Peetham pontiff. Built in the Dravidian style with sculptures by TTD's own SVITSA heritage wing, it follows Vaikhanasa Agama rituals on the Tirumala model, including daily Suprabhatam, Thomala, Sahasranama Archana and Naivedyam sevas.

name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Visakhapatnam (Vizag), on the Bay of Bengal coast, is the largest city of Andhra Pradesh and a major port and naval hub (home to the Eastern Naval Command, Visakhapatnam Port and a steel plant), often called the 'City of Destiny'. It blends beaches (RK Beach, Rushikonda Beach) with hilltop attractions like Kailasagiri and the INS Kursura submarine museum, and nearby pilgrimage sites such as Simhachalam. The Rushikonda temple sits on the hill above Rushikonda Beach, about 10 km from RK Beach along the coastal road.

travel.airport: Visakhapatnam International Airport (VTZ) (approx. 22 km via NH16; taxis, app cabs and airport buses available).
travel.railway: Visakhapatnam Junction (VSKP) (approx. 15 km via Beach Road or NH16), well connected to Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Chennai, Bengaluru and Delhi.
travel.road: The temple is on the Rushikonda hill, about 1.2 km uphill from Rushikonda Beach and approx. 13 km from the RTC Complex (Dwaraka Bus Station). APSRTC buses, auto-rickshaws and cabs ply to Rushikonda Beach; a motorable road leads up to the temple, and parking is available at the complex.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the coastal weather is coolest. Early morning (Suprabhatam) and sunset darshan are the most pleasant; weekdays have shorter queues. Festival days (Ekadasi, Kalyanotsavam, 2nd-Saturday laddu day) draw crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM (verify - one source lists closing at 8:30 PM). Detailed seva schedule: Suprabhatam 6:00-6:30 AM, Viswaroopa Darshan 6:30-8:00 AM, Thomala 8:00-8:30 AM, Sahasranama Archana 8:30-9:00 AM, Naivedyam 9:00-9:30 AM, Sarva Darshan 9:30 AM-12 noon, break 12 noon-1:00 PM, Sarva Darshan 1:00-6:00 PM, Naivedyam 6:00-7:00 PM, Sarva Darshan 7:00-8:00 PM, Ekanta Seva 8:00-8:30 PM. Sarva darshan is free; photography is restricted inside the sanctum.
